name: T3 / thyroid fat loss

card.summary: Using the thyroid hormone liothyronine (T3) off-label to cut body fat; the drug label says it is ineffective for weight loss at normal doses and risky at high ones.
card.note: The prescribing label warns that larger doses in people with normal thyroid function can cause serious toxicity.

quick.overview:
T3 is the active thyroid hormone, available by prescription as liothyronine for hypothyroidism. In bodybuilding and cutting circles it has been used off-label in the hope of raising metabolic rate and losing fat.

There is little looksmaxxing-specific documentation. The regulatory label states that, in people with normal thyroid function, ordinary hormone-range doses are ineffective for weight reduction.
quick.mechanism: T3 raises basal metabolic rate, affects protein synthesis and increases sensitivity to catecholamines such as adrenaline.
quick.risks: Excess thyroid hormone can cause sweating, tremor, insomnia, arrhythmias and heart failure. The label warns of serious or life-threatening toxicity at larger doses, especially alongside sympathomimetic amines. It is prescription-only in the UK and Canada.

lead: Liothyronine is a synthetic form of triiodothyronine (T3), the more active of the two main thyroid hormones. It was approved for medical use in 1956 and is used mainly for hypothyroidism and myxedema coma.[1]

In bodybuilding and physique circles, T3 (often by its brand name Cytomel) is taken off-label during a cut with the aim of a leaner, more defined look: the idea is that thyroid hormone raises basal metabolic rate and fat oxidation, so more body fat is lost while dieting.[2][3] Wikipedia's article on T3 confirms that the hormone increases basal metabolic rate and stimulates lipid breakdown.[2]

The prescribing information for liothyronine states that in people with normal thyroid function, normal-range doses are ineffective for weight reduction and that larger doses can be seriously toxic.[1] Competition rules for some natural bodybuilding federations list T3 and T4 among prohibited substances.[5]

chain: T3 raises basal metabolic rate and lipid breakdown
More energy expended during a calorie deficit
angle.text: Bodybuilders add T3 to a cutting phase hoping to raise energy expenditure and fat loss so muscle definition shows sooner. Thyroid hormone does raise metabolic rate physiologically, though the drug label states that ordinary doses are ineffective for weight reduction in people with normal thyroid function.

paras: Liothyronine is prescribed for hypothyroidism and myxedema coma, and may be considered where peripheral conversion of T4 to T3 is poor. It has also been used in thyroid cancer care and as an add-on to some antidepressants.[1]

Liothyronine increases basal metabolic rate, influences protein synthesis and increases sensitivity to catecholamines. It has a faster onset and shorter half-life than levothyroxine.[1] T3 raises oxygen and energy consumption and speeds turnover of macromolecules; for proteins it increases synthesis, though in excess breakdown can outpace it.[2]

sections.h: Use for fat loss in physique culture
paras: A T Nation steroid overview from 2003 lists Cytomel as a synthetic thyroid hormone used by bodybuilders, noting suppression of the body's own thyroid function during use.[3] Participants in T Nation threads discuss thyroid markers such as free T3 and reverse T3 and the fast action of liothyronine compared with levothyroxine.[4][6]

The product's boxed warning says that doses within the normal daily hormone range are ineffective for weight reduction in euthyroid people, and that larger doses may produce serious or life-threatening toxicity, particularly when taken with sympathomimetic amines.[1] Use for obesity is not recommended.[1]

Side effects resemble hyperthyroidism and include sweating, nervousness, heat sensitivity and weight loss; less common effects include diarrhea, headache, insomnia, tremor, irritability and menstrual changes. Excess doses can cause arrhythmias and heart failure. It is contraindicated in thyrotoxicosis and uncorrected adrenal insufficiency.[1]

No studies found on T3 for cosmetic or looksmaxxing fat loss in people with normal thyroid function. Related human research includes a randomized trial of the acute effects of liothyronine on the cardiovascular system and energy metabolism in healthy volunteers, and trials of levothyroxine plus liothyronine in hypothyroidism.[7][8]

lore.intro: T3 comes up in bodybuilding forums as a cutting aid and as part of discussions about thyroid lab values.[3][4]

claims.claim: T3 speeds fat loss during a cut
claims.believers: Forum overviews list Cytomel as a synthetic thyroid hormone used by bodybuilders to raise metabolism while dieting.[3]
claims.experts: The drug label states that normal-range doses are ineffective for weight reduction in euthyroid people and that larger doses can be seriously toxic.[1]

claims.claim: Free T3 should be near the top of range, and reverse T3 can blunt T3 effects
claims.believers: T Nation posters advise checking free T3 and reverse T3 when fatigued.[6]
claims.experts: No published trial in healthy people tests this for physique outcomes; clinical research addresses hypothyroidism.[7][8]
